messages:
Vikram Singh: Dropping ADR draft for Shadow Traffic mirroring arch (ADR-0241). Would love review from arch + sec + obs folks. Main open questions called out: (1) retention/logging, (2) request replay safety, (3) deterministic policy evaluation for joins + future analysis.
Link: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/adr-0241-shadow-traffic-mirroring

Ethan Park: skimming now. One immediate thing: we need to be explicit what we mean by “replay” vs “mirror”. The queue-based design is *not* replaying the original external request, it’s enqueuing an internal “shadow job” built from a sanitized snapshot. Otherwise people will assume all headers/body etc are persisted.

Emily Zhao: +1. also note we need hard guarantees on not reusing auth/context. e.g. don’t forward customer `Authorization` or session cookies to shadow target. Build a new internal request w/ `request_id` + normalized prompt payload only.

Naomi Feldman: From security side: please tighten the language in retention section. I’m seeing “store inputs/outputs for debugging” — that reads like “we can keep prompts” by default. For SOC2 + privacy posture we need:
- default = do not persist raw prompt/output content
- if enabled, it must be opt-in per customer + per route, with retention cap + residency enforcement
- outputs used for LLM-as-judge should be treated as restricted data; access controls + audit log required

Logan Wright: For telemetry, we can do metrics-only by default (aggregated counters/hists). But for eval signals like similarity / format adherence, do we need storing the *shadow output* to compute later? If scoring happens inline in shadow runner we can just emit scores + token counts and never store payload.

Allison Grant: please call out “no high-cardinality tags from payload” in ADR. We already got burned on metrics explosions in similar features. If we need per-request debugging, that should be in traces with sampling + strict allowlist.

Ravi Menon: deterministic policy evaluation: I want to avoid “evaluate policy twice” with different outcomes (e.g. dynamic capacity signals, time-based rules). If primary and shadow selection uses policy engine at different times, the shadow target can drift.
Suggestion: primary path computes `shadow_plan` (targets + sampling decision + policy_version/hash) deterministically and attaches to the shadow job. Shadow runner executes that plan without re-evaluating.

Mina Haddad: +1 to Ravi. Smart routing has a bunch of dynamic inputs (region load, failover state). We should freeze routing decisions for *shadow* at request time, otherwise comparisons are messy.

Benji Okafor: + freezing plan is doable in RoutePolicy. We can have fields like:
- `policy_revision_id`
- `shadow_sampling_decision` (bool + reason)
- `shadow_targets_resolved` (list of target ids)
But we need to be careful about serializing “resolved targets” across deploys (schema evolution). Maybe only store stable target identifiers and runtime resolves to concrete model endpoint.

Marissa Cole: (product angle) We need “why did this request get shadowed?” and “what shadow target did it go to?” visible in Console when debugging. So +1 on including the plan + reason codes.
But I’m aligned with “don’t persist prompts by default”. Customers are already asking.

Rafael Mendes: replay safety: can we guarantee that tool calls / function calling won’t side-effect? If shadow is executing the same request, candidate model may attempt tool calls (webhooks etc). We need a mechanism to disable tool execution in shadow runs or route tool calls to a null tool handler.

Emily Zhao: yep. We should implement “shadow mode” in inference runtime: tool calling allowed only in “dry_run” mode. I’d like this explicitly in ADR as a requirement, otherwise someone will enable shadow on a route w/ tools and we’ll trigger external actions.

Ethan Park: Also for OpenAI-compat layer: ensure we strip user-supplied `seed`? Wait, opposite: we might need to *preserve* the seed to make A/B deterministic where possible. But lots of models ignore it. ADR should clarify expectations: determinism best-effort, but policy selection determinism must be hard.

Logan Wright: On retention: if we do judge scoring inside shadow runner, we do need to pass the candidate output into judge prompt, but we don’t need to store it. The judge request itself is another model call though—same residency issues apply.
Question: do we allow judge in different region? I’d say no: judge must run in same residency boundary as the shadow output.

Naomi Feldman: Agree: judge must respect same residency boundary. And we should define “residency boundary” concretely in ADR (e.g., EU-only, US-only). Also call out redaction pre-judge: even if we don’t store, we’re still transmitting to judge model.

Allison Grant: +1. And if judge scoring is optional, we should default it off for beta unless customer explicitly enables, because it adds cost + latency to shadow job. (shadow latency doesn’t hit end user but impacts capacity budgets).

Ravi Menon: Another determinism issue: sampling. If sampling uses RNG per pod, then primary and shadow logging can diverge (and it’ll look like “missing shadow data”). Use `request_id` hashed with a stable salt (per customer+route) so decision is deterministic + explainable.

Benji Okafor: yep, we can implement sampling as `hash(request_id, customer_id, route_id, salt) < pct`. Store `sampling_salt_id` in policy so we can rotate if needed.

Vikram Singh: This is super helpful. I’ll update ADR with:
- terminology: mirror -> build internal shadow job; avoid “replay” phrasing
- “shadow_plan” computed on primary path including policy_revision_id + target ids + sampling decision/reason
- tool calling dry-run / null tool handler requirement
- retention defaults + opt-in only, no raw payload persistence by default
- judge runs in same residency boundary + redaction before judge
- deterministic sampling via request_id hash + salt

Jordan Lee: minor: make sure “policy_revision_id” is immutable and stored alongside the job event so joins are possible later even if route policy changes. We’ll want to segment metrics by the policy revision in analytics.

Naomi Feldman: please add one more: if customer opts into payload logging for troubleshooting, require explicit retention window (e.g. 7d max by default) + access via restricted role, audited. Also mention “customer opt-out / disable at any time” including kill switch.

Rafael Mendes: and from oncall POV: add note that if queue backs up we drop shadow jobs (w/ counter) rather than retrying forever. That’s part of “safety” too.

Allison Grant: + when dropping, emit `shadow_eval.drop_count` with reason tags only from allowlist (budget_exceeded, queue_full, kill_switch, policy_disabled) etc.

Vikram Singh: ack. I’ll post revised ADR link in this thread later today for final sign-off.
